timeline_list.title: Classic Scorsese
timeline_list.description: With GoodFellas (1990), Martin Scorsese (b. 1942) is considered to have returned to form.

timeline_list.title: Julia Roberts' charm wins over the world
timeline_list.description: Pretty Woman (1990) hits theaters, becoming a huge success and introducing Julia Roberts (b. 1967) to the world. The film paved the way for a new era of romantic comedies in the 1990s and 2000s.

timeline_list.title: New Zealand to the World
timeline_list.description: An Angel at My Table (1990) is the first New Zealand film to be screened at the Venice Film Festival. It receives the Grand Special Jury Prize.

timeline_list.title: A raw, unvarnished reality
timeline_list.description: Boyz n the Hood (1991), by John Singleton (1968-2019), is one of the best African American films of the decade.

timeline_list.title: The Disney Renaissance
timeline_list.description: Beauty and the Beast (1991) hits theaters and earns a Best Picture nomination, a first for an animated film. The film also marked the beginning of a new golden age of Walt Disney animation.

timeline_list.title: The power of CGI draws attention
timeline_list.description: The liquid-metal killer capable of taking on different forms in Terminator 2: Judgment Day (1991) shows that CGI can create great monsters.

timeline_list.title: Sundance Film Festival
timeline_list.description: The Utah Film Festival takes on the name Sundance Film Festival: a brand is born.

timeline_list.title: Malcolm X through Spike Lee's lens
timeline_list.description: Malcolm X (1992), a powerful film biography by Spike Lee (b. 1957), flirts with controversy by using footage of the violence against Rodney King in its opening credits.

timeline_list.title: The Cinema of Quentin Tarantino
timeline_list.description: Quentin Tarantino (b. 1963) makes Reservoir Dogs (1992) and becomes one of the most influential filmmakers of the decade.

timeline_list.title: Dinosaurs like never before
timeline_list.description: Jurassic Park (1993) hits theaters and earns 3 Oscar nominations. To this day, the film still impresses with its special effects.

timeline_list.title: Spielberg's prestige
timeline_list.description: Schindler's List (1993) dominates the Oscars, and Steven Spielberg (b. 1946) is finally recognized as a serious filmmaker.

timeline_list.title: Hakuna Matata!
timeline_list.description: The Lion King (1994) is released, becoming the highest-grossing hand-drawn animated film in history.

timeline_list.title: Four Weddings and a Funeral
timeline_list.description: Four Weddings and a Funeral (1994) becomes the highest-grossing British film up to that time, earning more than $245.7 million worldwide.

timeline_list.title: Stop-motion
timeline_list.description: The Nightmare Before Christmas (1993) is released, directed by Tim Burton. The film became a hit and a driving force behind future successes in stop-motion animation.

timeline_list.title: Ghost in the Shell
timeline_list.description: Ghost in the Shell (1995) shows Oshii Mamoru's (b. 1951) intention to use animation to tackle more adult themes.

timeline_list.title: 3D animation
timeline_list.description: Pixar's Toy Story (1995) becomes the first of many successful CGI animated feature films. The process all but replaces conventional 2D animation.

timeline_list.title: Dogme 95
timeline_list.description: Directors Lars von Trier (b. 1956) and Thomas Vinterberg (b. 1969) sign the Dogme 95 Manifesto in Paris.

timeline_list.title: Scream
timeline_list.description: Scream (1996) reinvents the slasher film. The Craft kicks off a series of soft horror films for teenagers.

timeline_list.title: Titanic
timeline_list.description: Titanic (1997) hits theaters and earns 14 Oscar nominations. The film grosses more than $2.1 billion, an unprecedented milestone in history up to that point.

timeline_list.title: J-Horror
timeline_list.description: Ringu (Ring, 1998) is an international hit, drawing attention to so-called J-horror.

timeline_list.title: Brazil is back in the game
timeline_list.description: Central do Brasil (Central Station, 1998) wins the Golden Bear at the Berlin Film Festival, reviving the prestige of Brazilian cinema around the world.

timeline_list.title: Dil Se...
timeline_list.description: Dil Se.. (1998) becomes the first Bollywood film to enter the UK top 10.

timeline_list.title: Found Footage
timeline_list.description: Shot on video, The Blair Witch Project (1999) becomes the first significant project to achieve major success thanks to promotion on the internet.

timeline_list.title: The Matrix and the new possibilities of CGI
timeline_list.description: The Matrix (1999) slows down time and explores computer-generated virtual reality.

timeline_list.title: Gross-Out Comedy
timeline_list.description: American Pie (1999) is released and becomes a huge box office hit. The film paved the way for the gross-out comedies that flooded theaters during the 2000s.

timeline_list.title: Martial Arts and Ang Lee
timeline_list.description: Ang Lee's (b. 1954) martial arts film Wo Hu Cang Long (Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon, 2000) becomes a huge hit, popularizing the genre around the world once again.

timeline_list.title: Iranian women
timeline_list.description: Dayereh (The Circle, 2000), a poignant film by Jafar Panahi about Iranian women, wins the FIPRESCI Prize and the Golden Lion at the Venice Film Festival.

timeline_list.title: The Return of Satirical Comedy
timeline_list.description: Scary Movie (2000) hits theaters, reviving the satirical comedy subgenre that began in the 1980s with Airplane! (1980).

timeline_list.title: X-Men
timeline_list.description: The success of X-Men (2000), directed by Bryan Singer (b. 1965), ushers in a new era of comic book adaptations.

timeline_list.title: New Mexican Cinema
timeline_list.description: Amores Perros (2000), by Alejandro González Iñárritu (b. 1963), and Y Tu Mamá También (2001), by Alfonso Cuarón (b. 1961), form the two faces of New Mexican Cinema.

timeline_list.title: The Latin American Masterpiece
timeline_list.description: Cidade de Deus (City of God, 2002) is released. The film becomes a hit and earns Oscar nominations.

timeline_list.title: Harry Potter
timeline_list.description: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (2001) is released, the start of one of the most popular young adult literary franchises in film, inspiring other adaptations for the screen.

timeline_list.title: The Dawn of Motion Capture
timeline_list.description: Gollum, in The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers (2002), is the first CGI-created character to appear in a mainstream film.

timeline_list.title: Studio Ghibli enchants the world
timeline_list.description: Sen to Chihiro no Kamikakushi (Spirited Away, 2001) is released, winning the Oscar and the Golden Bear. Its success elevates the name of Studio Ghibli.

timeline_list.title: Korean cinema catches the world's attention
timeline_list.description: Oldboy (2003) catches the world's attention at the Cannes Film Festival, earning high praise from Quentin Tarantino (b. 1963).

timeline_list.title: With great power comes great responsibility
timeline_list.description: Sam Raimi's (b. 1959) Spider-Man (2002) is released. The film changes the landscape of superhero movie adaptations, keeping the humanization brought by the X-Men franchise films while adding the color of the comic books.

timeline_list.title: A phenomenon called The Lord of the Rings
timeline_list.description: The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King (2003) is the most successful film in the series and sweeps up a total of 11 Oscars.

timeline_list.title: Splatter
timeline_list.description: The Saw franchise kicks off the popularity of the splatter subgenre.

timeline_list.title: Marvel Cinematic Universe
timeline_list.description: Iron Man (2008) is released, launching its Cinematic Universe. Underestimated at first, within a few years every studio would be trying to develop a similar Shared Universe on the big screen.

timeline_list.title: The Dark Knight
timeline_list.description: The Dark Knight (2008) is the year's biggest box office hit. The film was one of the first to be shot with IMAX cameras, and it earned 8 Oscar nominations, winning Best Supporting Actor for Heath Ledger (1979-2008), something unprecedented for a superhero film at the time.

timeline_list.title: Paranormal Activity
timeline_list.description: Paranormal Activity (2007) becomes one of the decade's biggest low-budget hits, popularizing found footage once and for all.

timeline_list.title: 3D
timeline_list.description: Avatar (2009) popularizes intensely CGI-rendered environments through a sophisticated 3D process. Pixar, DreamWorks, and others follow the same path.
